01
Before the first verse · Vol. 4, p. 761

Opening of the surah

Vol. 4, p. 761
Surah al-Layl. Meccan; its verses: 21. “Revealed after al-Aʿlā.” In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة الليل مكية، وآياتها 21 «نزلت بعد الأعلى» بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
02
Q 92:1–4 · Vol. 4, pp. 761–762

Verses 1 to 4

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the night when it covers (1) And the day when it appears (2) And He who created the male and the female (3) Indeed, your efforts are diverse (4)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشى (1) وَالنَّهارِ إِذا تَجَلَّى (2) وَما خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى (3) إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى (4)
Vol. 4, p. 761
The thing covered is either the sun, from His saying “and the night when it covers it,” or the day, from His saying “He covers the night with the day,” or everything that [the night] veils with its darkness, from His saying “when it settles.” “When it appears”: it became manifest with the departure of the darkness of night; or it became clear and uncovered with the rising of the sun. “And He who created”: the One of great power who was able to create the male and the female from a single water. It is also said: they are Adam ﷺ and Eve. In the reading of the Prophet ﷺ: “and the male and the female.” And Ibn Masʿūd read: “wa-lladhī khalaqa l-dhakara wa-l-unthā” [“and He who created the male and the female”].
المغشى: إما الشمس من قوله وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشاها وإما النهار من قوله يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ وإما كل شيء يواريه بظلامه من قوله إِذا وَقَبَ. تَجَلَّى ظهر بزوال ظلمة الليل. أو تبين وتكشف بطلوع الشمس وَما خَلَقَ والقادر العظيم القدرة الذي قدر على خلق الذكر والأنثى من ماء واحد. وقبل: هما آدم عليه السلام وحواء. وفي قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: والذكر والأنثى. وقرأ ابن مسعود: والذي خلق الذكر والأنثى.
Vol. 4, p. 762
And from al-Kisāʾī: “wa-mā khalaqa l-dhakari wa-l-unthā,” with jarr, as a substitution for the locus of “mā khalaqa,” in the sense “and what God created,” i.e., “and God's creation, the male and the female.” It is permissible to suppress the name of God because it is known, through His uniqueness in creating, since there is no creator other than Him. It is also said: God did not create any creature among the ensouled that is neither male nor female. The hermaphrodite (khunthā), though his case is ambiguous to us, is not ambiguous to God, being known as male or female; so if one swore by divorce that he did not meet that day a male or a female, and he did meet an ambiguous hermaphrodite, he would be in breach of his oath, because in reality he is either male or female, even if ambiguous to us. “Lashattā”: plural of shatīt, i.e., your efforts are scattered and diverse, and the explanation of their diversity is in what He detailed after it.
وعن الكسائي: وما خلق الذكر والأنثى بالجر على أنه بدل من محل ما خَلَقَ بمعنى: وما خلقه الله، أى: ومخلوق الله الذكر والأنثى. وجاز إضمار اسم الله لأنه معلوم لانفراده بالخلق. إذ لا خالق سواه. وقيل: إنّ الله لم يخلق خلقا من ذوى الأرواح ليس بذكر ولا أنثى. والخنثى، وإن أشكل أمره عندنا فهو عند الله غير مشكل، معلوم بالذكورة أو الأنوثة، فلو حلف بالطلاق أنه لم يلق يومه ذكرا ولا أنثى، ولقد لقى خنثى مشكلا: كان حانثا، لأنه في الحقيقة إمّا ذكرا أو أنثى، وإن كان مشكلا عندنا لَشَتَّى جمع شتيت، أى: إنّ مساعيكم أشتات مختلفة، وبيان اختلافها فيما فصل على أثره.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 762
1. (1) . Agreed upon, from the ḥadīth of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and from the ḥadīth of ʿAlī ؓ.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Easing toward ease is the creation of graces … etc.” Aḥmad said: He does not lengthen his tongue here against Ahl al-Sunna, but the truth has restrained him; so you see him interpreting the speech — indeed, nullifying it — because he loads it with what it cannot bear; and upon his speech in such [verses] is the alarm of a frightened thief.
1. (1) . متفق عليه من حديث عمران بن حصين، ومن حديث على رضى الله عنه.
2. . قال محمود: «التيسير لليسرى خلق الألطاف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: ألا يطيل لسانه هاهنا على أهل السنة ولكن قصره الحق فتراه يؤول الكلام بل يعطله، لأنه يحمله مالا يحتمله، وعلى كلامه في أمثالها روعة السارق الخائف.
03
Q 92:5–7 · Vol. 4, p. 762

Verses 5 to 7

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So as for he who gives and fears God (5) And believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7)
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطى وَاتَّقى (5) وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى (6) فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرى (7)
Vol. 4, p. 762
“Gives” — meaning the due rights of his wealth; “and fears God” — so he did not disobey Him; “and believes in the best” — the best attribute, which is faith; or the best creed, which is the creed of Islam; or the best reward, which is Paradise. “We will ease him toward ease”: We will prepare him for it, from “yassara l-faras” [“he made the horse ready”] for riding, when he saddles and bridles it. From it is the saying of him ﷺ: “Everyone is made easy for that for which he was created” [1]. The meaning: We will deal gently with him and grant him success until obedience becomes the easiest and lightest of matters for him [2], from His saying “Whomever God wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam.”
أَعْطى يعنى حقوق ماله وَاتَّقى الله فلم يعصه وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى بالخصلة الحسنى: وهي الإيمان. أو بالملة الحسنى: وهي ملة الإسلام، أو بالمثوبة الحسنى: وهي الجنة فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرى فسنهيؤه لها من يسر الفرس للركوب إذا أسرجها وألجمها. ومنه قوله عليه السلام: «كل ميسر لما خلق «1» له» والمعنى: فسنلطف به ونوفقه حتى تكون الطاعة أيسر الأمور عليه وأهونها «2» ، من قوله فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلامِ.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 762
1. (1) . Agreed upon, from the ḥadīth of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and from the ḥadīth of ʿAlī ؓ.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Easing toward ease is the creation of graces … etc.” Aḥmad said: He does not lengthen his tongue here against Ahl al-Sunna, but the truth has restrained him; so you see him interpreting the speech — indeed, nullifying it — because he loads it with what it cannot bear; and upon his speech in such [verses] is the alarm of a frightened thief.
1. (1) . متفق عليه من حديث عمران بن حصين، ومن حديث على رضى الله عنه.
2. . قال محمود: «التيسير لليسرى خلق الألطاف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: ألا يطيل لسانه هاهنا على أهل السنة ولكن قصره الحق فتراه يؤول الكلام بل يعطله، لأنه يحمله مالا يحتمله، وعلى كلامه في أمثالها روعة السارق الخائف.
04
Q 92:8–11 · Vol. 4, pp. 762–763

Verses 8 to 11

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need (8) And denies the best (9) We will ease him toward difficulty (10) And his wealth will not avail him when he falls (11)
وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنى (8) وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنى (9) فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى (10) وَما يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مالُهُ إِذا تَرَدَّى (11)
Vol. 4, p. 762
“And considers himself free of need”: he is indifferent to what is with God, as if he were independent of Him, and so did not fear Him; or he considered himself independent, through the desires of this world, of the bliss of Paradise, because it stands in contrast to “and fears God.” “We will ease him toward difficulty”: We will forsake him and withhold the graces from him until obedience becomes the hardest and most severe thing for him, from His saying “He makes his breast tight and constricted as if he were ascending into the sky”; or He called the way of good “ease” because its outcome is ease, and the way of evil “difficulty” because its outcome is difficulty; or He meant by them the two roads of Paradise and the Fire, i.e.: We shall guide them in the Hereafter to the two roads. It is also said: the two [groups of verses] were revealed about Abū Bakr ؓ and about Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb. “And what avails him” is an interrogative in the sense of denial, or a negation. “When he falls (taraddā)”: [the form] tafaʿʿala from radā, which is destruction, meaning death; or he fell into the pit when buried; or he fell into the bottom of Hell.
وَاسْتَغْنى وزهد فيما عند الله كأنه مستغن عنه فلم يتقه. أو استغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم الجنة، لأنه في مقابلة وَاتَّقى. فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى فسنخذله ونمنعه الألطاف، حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشدّه، من قوله يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرَجاً كَأَنَّما يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّماءِ أو سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى، لأنّ عاقبتها اليسر، وطريقة الشر العسرى، لأن عاقبتها العسر. أو أراد بهما طريقى الجنة والنار، أى: فسنهديهما في الآخرة للطريقين. وقيل: نزلتا في أبى بكر رضى الله عنه، وفي أبى سفيان بن حرب وَما يُغْنِي عَنْهُ استفهام في معنى الإنكار، أو نفى تَرَدَّى تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك، يريد: الموت. أو تردّى في الحفرة إذا قبر. أو تردى في قعر جهنم.
Vol. 4, p. 763
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 762
1. (1) . Agreed upon, from the ḥadīth of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and from the ḥadīth of ʿAlī ؓ.
2. . Maḥmūd said: “Easing toward ease is the creation of graces … etc.” Aḥmad said: He does not lengthen his tongue here against Ahl al-Sunna, but the truth has restrained him; so you see him interpreting the speech — indeed, nullifying it — because he loads it with what it cannot bear; and upon his speech in such [verses] is the alarm of a frightened thief.
1. (1) . متفق عليه من حديث عمران بن حصين، ومن حديث على رضى الله عنه.
2. . قال محمود: «التيسير لليسرى خلق الألطاف
…. الخ» قال أحمد: ألا يطيل لسانه هاهنا على أهل السنة ولكن قصره الحق فتراه يؤول الكلام بل يعطله، لأنه يحمله مالا يحتمله، وعلى كلامه في أمثالها روعة السارق الخائف.
Vol. 4, p. 763
1. (1) . His statement “lahu wājib ʿalaynā bi-naṣb al-dalāʾil” [as printed]: the obligation of anything upon God Exalted is the doctrine of the Muʿtazila. Nothing is obligatory upon Him according to Ahl al-Sunna, but it is the way of the Generous to confirm a promise. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “If you ask: how did He say ‘None will burn in it except the most wretched … and the most pious will be kept away from it,’ when it is known that every wretched person burns in it … etc.” Aḥmad said: There is no doubt that the questioner built his question on relying upon the implied meaning (mafhūm) of the verse, because it came in the form of restriction; so the gist of al-Zamakhsharī's answer is that the restriction here is for a benefit other than negating [the ruling] from everything besides the restricted item, and that benefit is contrast (muqābala). And since the question and the answer have become clear to you, he is keeping an eye on the view of al-Shāfiʿī ؒ regarding the saying of God Exalted: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it”; for he did not hold the implied meaning of its restriction, and took it that the restriction is for the benefit of contrast, by way of refutation of the rulings of the Jāhiliyya, not to negate anything outside what is restricted. Moreover, al-Zamakhsharī was pressed in this verse until he committed himself to the occurrence of the mentioned question, out of regard for his corrupt principle and his fear that it would be broken; but God refuses except to break it and reject it. And if the verse is brought down upon the principles of Ahl al-Sunna, what I have said becomes clear to you. So we say: “muṣallā” in the language is [what results] when they dig a pit and gather in it many burning coals, then proceed to a sheep and bury it in the midst of them between their layers; whereas what is roasted above the coals, or on a griddle, or in an oven, is not “muṣallā.” This very interpretation was stated explicitly by al-Zamakhsharī and transmitted by him from the people of the language in Sūrat al-Ghāshiya as well, and I myself have come upon it in their books. So if you know the meaning of taṣliya in language, and that it is the most intense kind of burning by fire, and you know that people, in the view of Ahl al-Sunna, are of three kinds — a righteous believer who is successful, a disobedient believer, and a disbeliever — and that the successful believer passes over the Fire and his light extinguishes its flame and he is in no way pained by its touch, and he comes to it only to fulfil the oath [taḥillat al-qasam]; and the disobedient one, if God wills to punish and requite him, is punished only on the surface of the Fire, in the first layer, by agreement — so that among them are those whom the fire reaches to the ankle, and the most severe of them are those whom the fire reaches to the place of his prostration, so he feels it — and no one among the believers is punished between its layers at all, by God's promise; and the disbeliever is the one punished between its layers: it becomes clear to you that none burns in the Fire — that is, is punished between its layers, as you have come to know its interpretation in the language — except the disbeliever, who is “the most wretched,” because the disobedient believer does not reach his degree in wretchedness; and that the successful believer, who is “the most pious” in relation to the disobedient believer, is kept away from the Fire entirely, because his coming to it is [only] to fulfil the oath and neither its touch nor its pain reaches him; and that the disobedient believer, who is neither the most pious nor the most wretched, neither burns in it nor is kept away from it entirely, because his coming [to it] is to fulfil the oath, but he is punished in it not by burning (ṣalā). This is the best of what the verse can be carried to, but it comes down only on the highway of the Sunna. As for al-Zamakhsharī, he deviates from it; so no wonder that he is, in the burden of the answer, thinking and estimating. And God knows best.
1. (1) . قوله «له واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل» وجوب شيء على الله تعالى: مذهب المعتزلة. ولا يجب عليه شيء عند أهل السنة، ولكن شأن الكريم تأكيد الوعد. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «فان قلت: كيف قال لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى وسيجنبها الأتقى، وقد علم أن كل شقى يصلاها
…. الخ» قال أحمد: لا شك أن السائل بنى سؤاله على التمسك بمفهوم الآية لورودها بصيغة التخصيص، فحاصل جواب الزمخشري أن التخصيص هاهنا لفائدة أخرى غير النفي عما عدا المخصص، وتلك الفائدة المقابلة، وحيث تمحض لك السؤال والجواب، فهو يلاحظ نظر الشافعي رحمه الله في قوله تعالى قُلْ لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ فانه لم يقل بمفهوم حصرها، وحملها على أن الحصر لفائدة المقابلة بالرد لأحكام الجاهلية، لا لنفى ما عدا المحصور. على أن الزمخشري إنما ضيق عليه الخناق في هذه الآية حتى التزم ورود السؤال المذكور، التفاته إلى قاعدته الفاسدة وحذره أن تنقض، ويأبى الله إلا نقضها ورفضها، وإذا نزلت الآية على قواعد أهل السنة وضع لك ما قلته، فنقول: المصلى في اللغة أن يحفروا حفيرا فيجمعوا فيه جمرا كثيرا، ثم يعمدوا إلى شاة فيدسوها وسطه بين أطباقه، فأما ما يشوى فوق الجمر أو على المقلى أو على التنور فليس بمصلى، وهذا التفسير بعينه نص عليه الزمخشري ونقطة عن أهل اللغة في سورة الغاشية أيضا، وأنا وقفت عليه في كتبهم، فإذا عرفت معنى التصلية لغة وأنها أشد أنواع الإحراق بالنار، وفي علمك أن الناس عند أهل السنة ثلاثة أصناف: مؤمن صالح فائز، ومؤمن عاص، وكافر، وأن المؤمن الفائز يمر على النار فيطفئ نوره لهبها ولا يؤلم بمسها البتة، وإنما يردها تحلة القسم، والعاصي إن شاء الله تعذيبه ومجازاته فإنما يعذب على وجه النار في الطبقة الأولى باتفاق، حتى أن منهم من تبلغ النار إلى كعبه: وأشدهم من تبلغ النار إلى موضع سجوده فيحسه، ولا يعذب أحد من المؤمنين بين أطباقها ألبتة بوعد الله تعالى، والكافر هو المعذب بين أطباقها: تبين لك أن النار لا يصلاها أى يعذب بين أطباقها- كما علمت تفسيره في اللغة- إلا الكافر: وهو الأشقى، لأن المؤمن العاصي لا يبلغ مبلغه في الشقاء، وأن المؤمن الفائز وهو الأتقى بالنسبة إلى المؤمن العاصي بجنب النار بالكلية، لأن وروده تحلة القسم لا يصل إليه مسها ولا ألمها، وأن المؤمن العاصي الذي ليس بالأتقى ولا بالأشقى لا يصلاها ولا يجنبها بالكلية، لأن وروده تحلة القسم بل يعذب فيها لا بالصلى، فهذا أحسن ما حملت الآية عليه، لكن إنما ينزل على جادة السنة. وأما الزمخشري فينحرف عنها، فلا جرم أنه في عهدة الجواب يفكر ويقدر. والله أعلم.
05
Q 92:12–13 · Vol. 4, p. 763

Verses 12 to 13

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Indeed upon Us is guidance (12) And indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life] (13)
إِنَّ عَلَيْنا لَلْهُدى (12) وَإِنَّ لَنا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولى (13)
Vol. 4, p. 763
“Indeed upon Us is guidance”: guiding to the truth is obligatory upon Us, by setting up proofs [1] and clarifying the laws. “And indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first”: i.e., the reward of both abodes for the one who is guided, as in His saying “And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed in the Hereafter he is among the righteous.”
إِنَّ عَلَيْنا لَلْهُدى إن الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل «1» وبيان الشرائع وَإِنَّ لَنا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولى أى ثواب الدّارين للمهتدى، كقوله وَآتَيْناهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 763
1. (1) . His statement “lahu wājib ʿalaynā bi-naṣb al-dalāʾil” [as printed]: the obligation of anything upon God Exalted is the doctrine of the Muʿtazila. Nothing is obligatory upon Him according to Ahl al-Sunna, but it is the way of the Generous to confirm a promise. (ʿ)

Moreover, al-Zamakhsharī was pressed in this verse until he committed himself to the occurrence of the mentioned question, out of regard for his corrupt principle and his fear that it would be broken; but God refuses except to break it and reject it. And if the verse is brought down upon the principles of Ahl al-Sunna, what I have said becomes clear to you. So we say: “muṣallā” in the language is [what results] when they dig a pit and gather in it many burning coals, then proceed to a sheep and bury it in the midst of them between their layers; whereas what is roasted above the coals, or on a griddle, or in an oven, is not “muṣallā.” This very interpretation was stated explicitly by al-Zamakhsharī and transmitted by him from the people of the language in Sūrat al-Ghāshiya as well, and I myself have come upon it in their books. So if you know the meaning of taṣliya in language, and that it is the most intense kind of burning by fire, and you know that people, in the view of Ahl al-Sunna, are of three kinds — a righteous believer who is successful, a disobedient believer, and a disbeliever — and that the successful believer passes over the Fire and his light extinguishes its flame and he is in no way pained by its touch, and he comes to it only to fulfil the oath [taḥillat al-qasam]; and the disobedient one, if God wills to punish and requite him, is punished only on the surface of the Fire, in the first layer, by agreement — so that among them are those whom the fire reaches to the ankle, and the most severe of them are those whom the fire reaches to the place of his prostration, so he feels it — and no one among the believers is punished between its layers at all, by God's promise; and the disbeliever is the one punished between its layers: it becomes clear to you that none burns in the Fire — that is, is punished between its layers, as you have come to know its interpretation in the language — except the disbeliever, who is “the most wretched,” because the disobedient believer does not reach his degree in wretchedness; and that the successful believer, who is “the most pious” in relation to the disobedient believer, is kept away from the Fire entirely, because his coming to it is [only] to fulfil the oath and neither its touch nor its pain reaches him; and that the disobedient believer, who is neither the most pious nor the most wretched, neither burns in it nor is kept away from it entirely, because his coming [to it] is to fulfil the oath, but he is punished in it not by burning (ṣalā). This is the best of what the verse can be carried to, but it comes down only on the highway of the Sunna. As for al-Zamakhsharī, he deviates from it; so no wonder that he is, in the burden of the answer, thinking and estimating. And God knows best.
1. (1) . قوله «له واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل» وجوب شيء على الله تعالى: مذهب المعتزلة. ولا يجب عليه شيء عند أهل السنة، ولكن شأن الكريم تأكيد الوعد. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «فان قلت: كيف قال لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى وسيجنبها الأتقى، وقد علم أن كل شقى يصلاها
…. الخ» قال أحمد: لا شك أن السائل بنى سؤاله على التمسك بمفهوم الآية لورودها بصيغة التخصيص، فحاصل جواب الزمخشري أن التخصيص هاهنا لفائدة أخرى غير النفي عما عدا المخصص، وتلك الفائدة المقابلة، وحيث تمحض لك السؤال والجواب، فهو يلاحظ نظر الشافعي رحمه الله في قوله تعالى قُلْ لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ فانه لم يقل بمفهوم حصرها، وحملها على أن الحصر لفائدة المقابلة بالرد لأحكام الجاهلية، لا لنفى ما عدا المحصور. على أن الزمخشري إنما ضيق عليه الخناق في هذه الآية حتى التزم ورود السؤال المذكور، التفاته إلى قاعدته الفاسدة وحذره أن تنقض، ويأبى الله إلا نقضها ورفضها، وإذا نزلت الآية على قواعد أهل السنة وضع لك ما قلته، فنقول: المصلى في اللغة أن يحفروا حفيرا فيجمعوا فيه جمرا كثيرا، ثم يعمدوا إلى شاة فيدسوها وسطه بين أطباقه، فأما ما يشوى فوق الجمر أو على المقلى أو على التنور فليس بمصلى، وهذا التفسير بعينه نص عليه الزمخشري ونقطة عن أهل اللغة في سورة الغاشية أيضا، وأنا وقفت عليه في كتبهم، فإذا عرفت معنى التصلية لغة وأنها أشد أنواع الإحراق بالنار، وفي علمك أن الناس عند أهل السنة ثلاثة أصناف: مؤمن صالح فائز، ومؤمن عاص، وكافر، وأن المؤمن الفائز يمر على النار فيطفئ نوره لهبها ولا يؤلم بمسها البتة، وإنما يردها تحلة القسم، والعاصي إن شاء الله تعذيبه ومجازاته فإنما يعذب على وجه النار في الطبقة الأولى باتفاق، حتى أن منهم من تبلغ النار إلى كعبه: وأشدهم من تبلغ النار إلى موضع سجوده فيحسه، ولا يعذب أحد من المؤمنين بين أطباقها ألبتة بوعد الله تعالى، والكافر هو المعذب بين أطباقها: تبين لك أن النار لا يصلاها أى يعذب بين أطباقها- كما علمت تفسيره في اللغة- إلا الكافر: وهو الأشقى، لأن المؤمن العاصي لا يبلغ مبلغه في الشقاء، وأن المؤمن الفائز وهو الأتقى بالنسبة إلى المؤمن العاصي بجنب النار بالكلية، لأن وروده تحلة القسم لا يصل إليه مسها ولا ألمها، وأن المؤمن العاصي الذي ليس بالأتقى ولا بالأشقى لا يصلاها ولا يجنبها بالكلية، لأن وروده تحلة القسم بل يعذب فيها لا بالصلى، فهذا أحسن ما حملت الآية عليه، لكن إنما ينزل على جادة السنة. وأما الزمخشري فينحرف عنها، فلا جرم أنه في عهدة الجواب يفكر ويقدر. والله أعلم.
06
Q 92:14–21 · Vol. 4, pp. 763–765

Verses 14 to 21

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So I have warned you of a fire blazing (14) None will burn in it except the most wretched (15) Who denied and turned away (16) And the most pious will be kept away from it (17) Who gives his wealth to purify himself (18) And no one has with him any favor to be repaid (19) Except seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (20) And he will surely be satisfied (21)
فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ ناراً تَلَظَّى (14) لا يَصْلاها إِلاَّ الْأَشْقَى (15) الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى (16) وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى (17) الَّذِي يُؤْتِي مالَهُ يَتَزَكَّى (18) وَما لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزى (19) إِلاَّ ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلى (20) وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضى (21)
Vol. 4, p. 763
Abū l-Zubayr read “tatalaẓẓā.” If you ask: how did He say “None will burn in it except the most wretched … and the most pious will be kept away from it,” when it is known that every wretched person burns in it [2], and every pious person is kept away from it — it is not the case that only the most wretched of the wretched burns, nor only the most pious of the pious is saved
وقرأ أبو الزبير: تتلظى. فإن قلت: كيف قال لا يَصْلاها إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى...... وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى وقد علم أن كل شقىّ يصلاها «2» ، وكل تقىّ يجنبها، لا يختص بالصلى أشقى الأشقياء، ولا بالنجاة
Vol. 4, p. 764
than the most pious of the pious; and if you claim that He made “the fire” indefinite and so meant a particular fire specific to the most wretched, then what will you do with His saying “and the most pious will be kept away from it” — for it is known that [even] the most sinful of the Muslims [1] is kept away from that particular fire, not merely the most pious of them? I say: the verse is delivered by way of balancing between the conditions of a great one among the polytheists and a great one among the believers; so it was intended to go to extremes in describing their two contradictory attributes. So “the most wretched” was said, and he was made specific to burning, as if the Fire had not been created but for him; and “the most pious” was said, and he was made specific to salvation, as if Paradise had not been created but for him. And it is said: they are Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf, and Abū Bakr ؓ. “Yatazakkā”: from zakāʾ, i.e., he seeks to be pure with God, intending by it neither display nor reputation; or it is of the form “yatafaʿʿalu” from zakāh.
أتقى الأتقياء، وإن زعمت أنه نكر النار فأراد نارا بعينها مخصوصة بالأشقى، فما تصنع بقوله وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى فقد علم أن أفسق المسلمين «1» يجنب تلك النار المخصوصة، لا الأتقى منهم خاصة؟ قلت: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين، فأريد أن يبالغ في صفتيهما المتناقضتين فقيل: الأشقى، وجعل مختصا بالصلى، كأن النار لم تخلق إلا له. وقيل: الأتقى، وجعل مختصا بالنجاة، كأن الجنة لم تخلق إلا له. وقيل: هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف، وأبو بكر رضى الله عنه يَتَزَكَّى من الزكاء. أى: يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكيا، لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة. أو يتفعل من الزكاة.
Question
If you ask: what is the locus (maḥall) of “yatazakkā”?
فإن قلت: ما محل يتزكى؟
Answer
I say: it has two aspects: if you make it a substitution for “yuʾtī,” it has no locus, because it enters into the ruling of the relative clause, and relative clauses have no locus; and if you make it a ḥāl from the pronoun in “yuʾtī,” its locus is accusative. “Ibtighāʾa wajhi rabbihi” is an exception from a different genus, namely favour, i.e., no one has with him any favour except seeking the face of his Lord — like your saying “there is no one in the house except a donkey.” Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read “illā btighāʾu wajhi rabbihi,” with raising, in the dialect of those who say “mā fī l-dāri aḥadun illā ḥimārun.” And he cited, for the two dialects, the verse of Bishr ibn Abī Ḥāzim: “It has become empty, desolate; no human is in it, / only gazelle fawns and ostriches moving to and fro” [2]; and the saying of the one who said: “And many a land with no human in it / except the wild gazelles (yaʿāfīr) and the white ones (ʿīs)” [3].
قلت: هو على وجهين: إن جعلته بدلا من يُؤْتِي فلا محل له لأنه داخل في حكم الصلة، والصلات لا محل لها وإن جعلته حالا من الضمير في يُؤْتِي فمحله النصب ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ مستثنى من غير جنسه وهو النعمة أى: ما لأحد عنده نعمة إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه، كقولك: ما في الدار أحد إلا حمارا وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب، إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه بالرفع: على لغة من يقول: ما في الدار أحد إلا حمار وأنشد في اللغتين قول بشر بن أبى حازم: أضحت خلاء قفارا لا أنيس بها … إلا الجآذر والظّلمان تختلف «2» وقول القائل: وبلدة ليس بها أنيس … إلّا اليعافير وإلّا العيس «3»
Vol. 4, p. 765
It is also possible that “ibtighāʾa wajhi rabbihi” is an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu) in meaning, because the meaning of the speech is: “he gives his wealth only seeking the face of his Lord, not to repay a favour.” “And he will surely be satisfied”: a promise of the reward that will please him and gladden his eye. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: “Whoever recites Sūrat wa-l-layl, God will give him until he is satisfied, and spare him hardship and ease for him ease” [1].
ويجوز أن يكون ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ مفعولا له على المعنى، لأنّ معنى الكلام: لا يؤتى ماله إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه، لا لمكافأة نعمة وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضى موعد بالثواب الذي يرضيه ويقرّ عينه. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة والليل، أعطاه الله حتى يرضى، وعافاه من العسر ويسر له اليسر» «1» .
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 763
1. (1) . His statement “lahu wājib ʿalaynā bi-naṣb al-dalāʾil” [as printed]: the obligation of anything upon God Exalted is the doctrine of the Muʿtazila. Nothing is obligatory upon Him according to Ahl al-Sunna, but it is the way of the Generous to confirm a promise. (ʿ)
2. . Maḥmūd said: “If you ask: how did He say ‘None will burn in it except the most wretched … and the most pious will be kept away from it,’ when it is known that every wretched person burns in it … etc.” Aḥmad said: There is no doubt that the questioner built his question on relying upon the implied meaning (mafhūm) of the verse, because it came in the form of restriction; so the gist of al-Zamakhsharī's answer is that the restriction here is for a benefit other than negating [the ruling] from everything besides the restricted item, and that benefit is contrast (muqābala). And since the question and the answer have become clear to you, he is keeping an eye on the view of al-Shāfiʿī ؒ regarding the saying of God Exalted: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it”; for he did not hold the implied meaning of its restriction, and took it that the restriction is for the benefit of contrast, by way of refutation of the rulings of the Jāhiliyya, not to negate anything outside what is restricted. Moreover, al-Zamakhsharī was pressed in this verse until he committed himself to the occurrence of the mentioned question, out of regard for his corrupt principle and his fear that it would be broken; but God refuses except to break it and reject it. And if the verse is brought down upon the principles of Ahl al-Sunna, what I have said becomes clear to you. So we say: “muṣallā” in the language is [what results] when they dig a pit and gather in it many burning coals, then proceed to a sheep and bury it in the midst of them between their layers; whereas what is roasted above the coals, or on a griddle, or in an oven, is not “muṣallā.” This very interpretation was stated explicitly by al-Zamakhsharī and transmitted by him from the people of the language in Sūrat al-Ghāshiya as well, and I myself have come upon it in their books. So if you know the meaning of taṣliya in language, and that it is the most intense kind of burning by fire, and you know that people, in the view of Ahl al-Sunna, are of three kinds — a righteous believer who is successful, a disobedient believer, and a disbeliever — and that the successful believer passes over the Fire and his light extinguishes its flame and he is in no way pained by its touch, and he comes to it only to fulfil the oath [taḥillat al-qasam]; and the disobedient one, if God wills to punish and requite him, is punished only on the surface of the Fire, in the first layer, by agreement — so that among them are those whom the fire reaches to the ankle, and the most severe of them are those whom the fire reaches to the place of his prostration, so he feels it — and no one among the believers is punished between its layers at all, by God's promise; and the disbeliever is the one punished between its layers: it becomes clear to you that none burns in the Fire — that is, is punished between its layers, as you have come to know its interpretation in the language — except the disbeliever, who is “the most wretched,” because the disobedient believer does not reach his degree in wretchedness; and that the successful believer, who is “the most pious” in relation to the disobedient believer, is kept away from the Fire entirely, because his coming to it is [only] to fulfil the oath and neither its touch nor its pain reaches him; and that the disobedient believer, who is neither the most pious nor the most wretched, neither burns in it nor is kept away from it entirely, because his coming [to it] is to fulfil the oath, but he is punished in it not by burning (ṣalā). This is the best of what the verse can be carried to, but it comes down only on the highway of the Sunna. As for al-Zamakhsharī, he deviates from it; so no wonder that he is, in the burden of the answer, thinking and estimating. And God knows best.

Vol. 4, p. 764
1. (1) . His statement “fa-qad ʿulima anna afsaq al-muslimīn”: perhaps [it should read] “wa-qad.” (ʿ)
2. . “It has become empty, desolate; no human is in it, / only gazelle fawns and ostriches moving to and fro. / I halted my young she-camel there that it might answer me, / or that the traces might tell of them, in which direction they departed” — by Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim [as printed]. “Khalāyā”: plural of khaliyya, i.e., empty. “Al-jāʾdhir and al-ẓulmān”: a disjoint exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because they are not included in “anīs.” It is related in the accusative as an exception, and with raising as a substitute for the pronoun implicit in the predicate, as is the dialect of Tamīm. “Al-jāʾdhir”: the young of wild cattle. It is also related “al-jawāzī”: those are gazelles that make do with eating spring herbage in place of drinking water. “Al-ẓulmān”: the young of ostriches, or the ostrich itself. “Al-qalūṣ”: the young she-camel, plump with flesh; the pronoun in “fīhā” refers to the abodes, and the pronoun of “tujāwibunī” refers to them as well. “Al-rasm”: the traces of the abodes. “Ayyata”: an interrogative noun, put in the accusative by what follows it, as an adverbial, because it is cut off from annexation, i.e., [in] which direction their resolve and intention turned them. He likened the traces to a rational being by way of the metaphor of implication (makniyya), and so ascribed to it informing by way of imagery (takhyīl); and likewise the abode and its responding.
3. . “We may leave the dwelling, O Lumays, / in which the loud-voiced beast of prey lives, / and many a land with no human in it / except the wild gazelles and except the white ones” — by ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥārith, known as Jirān al-ʿAwd. Lumays: a woman. Al-jarūs: of loud voice. “Baldatin” — in the genitive by an implied “rubba” after the wāw, i.e.: we may leave the dwelling empty of its people, either by our killing them or by our departure from them. “Al-yaʿāfīr” — in the nominative —: a substitute for “anīs” in the dialect of Tamīm in the disjoint exception after a negation; and the second “illā” is a corroboration of the first. “Al-yaʿāfīr” — plural of yaʿfūr: an animal the size of a lamb, ash-coloured. It is also said: a gazelle, likewise. It is also said: the young of the wild cow. “Al-ʿīs”: the white ones among gazelles or camels — plural of aʿyas or ʿaysāʾ. And al-ʿaysāʾ is also the female locust, whose whiteness is mingled with a tawny colour.
1. (1) . قوله «فقد علم أن أفسق المسلمين» لعله: وقد. (ع)
2. . أضحت خلايا قفارا لا أنيس بها
…. إلا الجاذر والظلمان تختلف رقفت فيها قلوصي كى تجاوبنى
…. أو بخبر الرسم عنهم أية انصرفوا لبشر بن أبى خازم. وخلايا: جمع خلية أى خالية، والجآذر والظلمان. استثناء منقطع، لأنها لا تدخل في الأنيس. ورويا بالنصب على الاستثناء، وبالرفع على الابدال من الضمير المستكن في الخير، كما هو لغة عند تميم. والجآذر: أولاد بقر الوحش. وروى: الجوازئ، رهى الظباء التي اجتزأت بأكل الربيع عن شرب الماء. والظلمان: أولاد النعام. أو النعام نفسه. والقلوص. الفتية من الإبل المكتنزة اللحم، والضمير فيها عائد للديار. وضمير «تجاوبنى» لها أيضا. والرسم: آثار الديار. وأية: اسم استفهام منصوب بما بعده على الظرفية، لقطعه عن الاضافة، أى: صرفهم عزمهم ونيتهم. وشبه الرسم بعاقل على طريق المكنية فأسند له الاخبار تخييلا، وكذلك الدار ومجاوبتها.
3. . قد ندع المنزل يا لميس
…. يعيش فيه السبع الجروس وبلدة ليس بها أنيس
…. إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس لعامر بن الحرث المشهور بجران العود. ولميس: امرأة. والجروس: كثير الصوت، وبلدة- بالجر برب المقدرة بعد الواو، أى: قد نترك المنزل خاليا من أهله بقتلنا إياهم، أو لارتحالنا عنهم. واليعافير- بالرفع-: بدل من أنيس على لغة تميم في الاستثناء المنقطع بعد النفي، وإلا الثانية توكيد للأولى. واليعافير- جمع يعفور-: دابة قدر السخلة على لون الرماد. وقيل: غزال كذلك. وقيل: ولد البقرة الوحشية. والعيس: البيض من الظباء أو الإبل: جمع أعيس أو عيساء. والعيساء أيضا: أنثى الجراد، يخالط بياضها شقرة.
Vol. 4, p. 765
1. (1) . Al-Thaʿlabī, al-Wāḥidī and Ibn Mardawayh reported it with the chain to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
1. (1) . أخرجه الثعلبي والواحدي وابن مردويه بالسند إلى أبى بن كعب.
